verdict.summary:
# Hydrostatic Leak Test Procedure - Water Manifold (Guarded Bench)

Document: HLT-WM-001 Rev A
Object under test: water manifold, already connected, initially unpressurized, on a guarded bench.
Medium: water. Test pressure: 6.00 bar gauge. Hold: 300 s isolated. Component rating: 10.0 bar gauge (all test components).

## 1. Scope
This procedure covers a hydrostatic leak test of the connected manifold from an unpressurized start to a 300 s isolated hold at 6.00 bar gauge, the pass/fail decision, and controlled depressurization to 0 bar gauge before disconnection.

## 2. Pressure envelope and safety basis
- Rating of all test components: 10.0 bar gauge.
- Maximum pressure permitted at any step of this procedure: 6.00 bar gauge. That is 60% of the 10.0 bar gauge rating, leaving a 4.00 bar margin to rating.
- Any over-pressure relief device fitted must be set above 6.00 bar gauge and at or below the lowest component rating.
- Bench guard in place before pressurization. Stay clear of the manifold plane during the hold. Safety glasses worn.
- No fitting is loosened or disconnected while the gauge reads above 0 bar gauge.

## 3. Instruments and materials
- Pressure gauge on the manifold side of the pump isolation valve, range 0-16 bar gauge (or the next standard range above the 10.0 bar gauge rating), resolution <= 0.02 bar, readable to 0.01 bar, calibrated; record gauge ID and calibration due date.
- Timer with 1 s resolution.
- Water supply, high-point vent, hand pump, pump isolation valve, release valve.
- Completed test log (section 7).

## 4. Procedure (execute in the order given)
1. Verify ratings: confirm the manifold, hoses, fittings, valves and gauge are each rated >= 10.0 bar gauge. If any item is unrated or rated below 10.0 bar gauge, stop; do not pressurize.
2. Confirm initial state: manifold connected, unpressurized, gauge reads 0.00 bar gauge, release valve closed, hand pump connected, high-point vent closed at this moment (it is opened in step 3). Record gauge ID and calibration due date.
3. Open the high-point vent fully.
4. Fill with water slowly through the fill path until water exits the high-point vent as a continuous, bubble-free stream; continue until bubble-free flow has persisted for at least 10 s so trapped air is purged.
5. Close the high-point vent while water is still present at the vent, so no air is drawn in. Dry the exterior of all joints so any later weep is visible.
6. Record the baseline: ambient temperature, water temperature (if measured), gauge reading (expected 0.00 bar gauge) and time.
7. Pressurize with the hand pump, slowly and in increments (guidance: 2 bar gauge per increment with a 15 s pause). Do not exceed 6.00 bar gauge at any time.
8. Stabilize at test pressure with the pump still connected: hold at 6.00 bar gauge until the reading is steady (change <= 0.05 bar over 30 s). Any top-up needed to reach or hold 6.00 bar gauge is permitted ONLY in this step, before isolation.
9. Set the final pre-isolation reading to exactly 6.00 bar gauge.
10. Isolate the hand pump: close the pump isolation valve fully so the pump is hydraulically disconnected from the manifold. Record the valve tag and confirm the closed position.
11. Start the hold timer ONLY NOW, after isolation is complete. Record t = 0 s and P_start = 6.00 bar gauge. Do not start the timer before step 10 is finished.
12. Hold for 300 s. During the hold: do NOT add water, do not operate the pump, and do not open, close or adjust any valve in the pressurized boundary. Inspect all joints, fittings, gauge connections and valve packings continuously for visible water leakage (weep, drip, mist, pooling).
13. At t = 300 s, stop the timer and record P_end in bar gauge, together with the leakage observation (none, or description and location).
14. Compute the pressure drop: dP = P_start - P_end, in bar.
15. Evaluate against the acceptance criteria in section 5 and record the verdict (PASS/FAIL) in the log.
16. Depressurize using the release valve: open it slowly and partially to vent at a controlled rate (guidance: no faster than about 1 bar/s). Do not disconnect anything while the manifold is pressurized.
17. Confirm 0 bar gauge: with the release path open to atmosphere, the gauge must read 0.00 bar gauge and remain at 0.00 bar gauge. If it does not fall to 0.00 bar gauge, stop - the release path is blocked or pressure is trapped; do not loosen any fitting.
18. Disconnect the manifold, drain and dry it, close the release valve, restore the bench, and file the completed log.

## 5. Acceptance criteria
- AC-1 (pressure retention): dP = P_start - P_end <= 0.20 bar across the 300 s isolated hold, with no water added during the hold.
- AC-2 (leakage): no visible water leakage at any point during the 300 s hold.
- Result rule: PASS only if AC-1 AND AC-2 are both met. Any visible water leakage is a FAIL regardless of dP. dP > 0.20 bar is a FAIL regardless of the leakage observation.

## 6. Verdict for the submitted log
| Item | Value | Criterion | Result |
|---|---|---|---|
| P_start at t = 0 s (after pump isolation) | 6.00 bar gauge | - | - |
| P_end at t = 300 s | 5.90 bar gauge | - | - |
| Pressure drop dP = 6.00 - 5.90 | 0.10 bar | <= 0.20 bar (AC-1) | Met, margin 0.10 bar (50% of allowance) |
| Visible water leakage during hold | None | None permitted (AC-2) | Met |
| Water added during hold | None | None permitted | Met |
| Test pressure vs component rating | 6.00 bar gauge vs 10.0 bar gauge | <= 10.0 bar gauge | Met, 4.00 bar margin |
| Depressurized via release valve | Yes | Required | Met |
| Gauge confirmed 0.00 bar gauge before disconnection | Yes | Required | Met |

Verdict: PASS. Both acceptance criteria are satisfied: the 0.10 bar drop is below the 0.20 bar limit, and no visible leakage occurred during the hold.

## 7. Completed test log (as recorded)
| Field | Entry |
|---|---|
| Test ID | HLT-WM-001-01 |
| Date / time hold started | (record) |
| Operator / witness | (record) |
| Gauge ID / calibration due | (record) |
| Component rating | 10.0 bar gauge |
| Fill bubble-free at high-point vent | Yes |
| High-point vent closed before pressurization | Yes |
| Pump isolated before timer start | Yes |
| P_start at t = 0 s | 6.00 bar gauge |
| P_end at t = 300 s | 5.90 bar gauge |
| Pressure drop dP | 0.10 bar |
| Visible leakage during hold | None |
| AC-1 (dP <= 0.20 bar) | Met |
| AC-2 (no visible leakage) | Met |
| Verdict | PASS |
| Depressurized via release valve | Yes |
| 0 bar gauge confirmed before disconnection | Yes |

## 8. Deviation and invalidation rules
- The run is INVALID and no verdict may be recorded if: the pump was not isolated before the timer started; water was added during the hold; the gauge is out of calibration; or the high-point vent was not closed before pressurization. Repeat from step 2 (or from step 7 if only the pressurization phase was affected).
- If the release valve cannot bring the gauge to 0.00 bar gauge, do not disconnect; stop and escalate.
- A FAIL requires investigation, repair, and a full retest under this procedure.

verdict.summary:
# Hydrostatic Leak-Test Procedure — Water Manifold on Guarded Bench

Item under test: water manifold, already connected, initially unpressurized (0 bar gauge). All test components rated 10.0 bar gauge. Test pressure 6.00 bar gauge = 60% of the 10.0 bar gauge rating.

## 1. Equipment and instruments

| Item | Requirement |
|---|---|
| Pressure gauge | 0–10 bar gauge range, resolution 0.05 bar or better, accuracy ±0.5% FS, calibration current (≤12 months), serial number recorded |
| Hand pump | Manual hydrostatic pump with its own isolation valve at the manifold test port, reservoir filled with clean water |
| Timer | Stopwatch or timer capable of 300 s ±1 s |
| Leak indicators | Dry white absorbent paper / tissue wrapped at every joint, thread and seal |
| Vent | High-point vent at the highest point of the manifold, operable and openable |
| Release valve | Dedicated depressurization valve discharging to drain, directed away from personnel |
| Thermometer | Ambient temperature at start and end of hold (recorded, not used for acceptance) |

## 2. Safety — guarded bench

- Perimeter guard/barrier in place with signage: "PRESSURE TEST IN PROGRESS — 6 bar WATER — DO NOT ENTER".
- PPE: safety glasses with side shields (face shield if any joint is within 300 mm of the operator's face), gloves, closed-toe footwear.
- No personnel in line with any threaded joint or plug during pressurization; operator stands to the side of the gauge, not over it.
- Release-valve discharge routed to drain, away from people and electrical equipment.
- Bench area clear of loose tooling; nothing stored above the manifold.

## 3. Acceptance criteria (defined before the test)

**AC-1 — Pressure retention.** Pressure drop over the 300 s isolated hold is no more than 0.20 bar: ΔP = P₀ − P₁ ≤ 0.20 bar, where P₀ is the gauge reading at the start of the isolated hold and P₁ the reading at 300 s. With P₀ = 6.00 bar gauge this is equivalent to P₁ ≥ 5.80 bar gauge.

**AC-2 — No visible leakage.** No visible water leakage at any joint, thread, seal, valve or component at any time during the 300 s hold (no droplets, mist, seepage, wetting of the indicator paper, or pooling).

**The test passes only if BOTH AC-1 and AC-2 are met.** Failure of either is a FAIL.

## 4. Ordered procedure

### Phase A — Preparation (manifold unpressurized)

1. Confirm the manifold is the correct item, all connections are made per drawing, and every test component is rated ≥ 10.0 bar gauge. Test pressure is 6.00 bar gauge; **do not exceed 6.00 bar gauge at any point in the test.**
2. Erect/verify the bench guard and signage; don PPE.
3. Verify and record the pressure gauge model, serial number, range (0–10 bar gauge), resolution, and calibration due date. Verify the timer.
4. Confirm the initial state: release valve OPEN, high-point vent OPEN, hand pump isolated from pressure, gauge reading **0 bar gauge**. If the gauge does not read 0 bar gauge, stop and resolve (gauge zero error or trapped pressure) before proceeding.
5. Dry all external surfaces. Wrap dry white absorbent paper or tissue around every joint, thread and seal to make any seepage visible.
6. Confirm the release-valve discharge is directed to drain, away from personnel and equipment.
7. Connect the hand pump to the fill/test port; pump isolation valve OPEN; reservoir filled with clean water.

### Phase B — Fill and vent (vent open)

8. Confirm the high-point vent is the highest point of the manifold and is fully open.
9. Fill slowly with water, vent open, at a rate that keeps the vent stream continuous and non-turbulent.
10. Continue filling until **bubble-free water exits the high-point vent in a continuous stream for at least 10 s.** Do not proceed until this is achieved. Gently tap high points of the manifold to release trapped air; if bubbles reappear, continue filling.
11. **Hold point H1:** bubble-free vent discharge confirmed; no air pockets remaining.
12. **Close the high-point vent** (hand-tight; do not over-torque). Record "vent closed" and the time. The vent remains closed for the remainder of the test.
13. Inspect all joints at static head for leakage. If leakage is present: stop, open the release valve, drain, repair, and restart from step 4.

### Phase C — Pressurization (staged, no overshoot)

14. Confirm release valve CLOSED, vent CLOSED, test-port plugs tight.
15. Pressurize in stages, slowly and monotonically, inspecting at each stage:
    - **Stage 1:** raise to 2.00 bar gauge; pause 30 s; inspect all joints and indicator paper.
    - **Stage 2:** raise to 4.00 bar gauge; pause 30 s; inspect all joints.
    - **Stage 3:** raise to 6.00 bar gauge; approach slowly and stop at 6.00 bar gauge — do not overshoot.
16. **Hold point H2:** gauge stable at 6.00 bar gauge and no visible leakage. Any visible leak at any stage → stop, go to step 26 (depressurize), record FAIL.
17. Any pressure drift while the pump is still connected may be corrected by pumping, but the correction must be recorded; the isolated hold (Phase D) always starts fresh after isolation.

### Phase D — Isolated hold, 300 s

18. **Isolate the hand pump:** close the pump isolation valve at the manifold test port (and disconnect the pump hose at that valve if the valve is not a proven shut-off) so the manifold is a closed volume. Record the isolation time.
19. **Start the 300 s hold timer only after isolation is complete.** Record t = 0 s and the gauge reading as **P₀**. P₀ shall read 6.00 bar gauge; if it differs from 6.00 bar gauge by more than the gauge resolution, re-establish 6.00 bar gauge, re-isolate, and restart this step (timer restarts at zero).
20. **During the 300 s hold: do not add water, do not operate the hand pump, do not open or close any valve, do not adjust any fitting.** The operator remains at the bench watching the gauge and all joints continuously.
21. Watch for visible water leakage at every joint, thread, seal, valve and component for the full 300 s. Record the time and location of any leak observed.
22. At t = 300 s, record the gauge reading immediately as **P₁**, without touching the pump or any valve. Record the ambient temperature.

### Phase E — Assessment (before depressurizing)

23. Compute the pressure drop: ΔP = P₀ − P₁.
24. Evaluate AC-1 (ΔP ≤ 0.20 bar) and AC-2 (no visible leakage) independently; record "met" or "not met" for each.
25. Declare the verdict: **PASS only if both AC-1 and AC-2 are met; otherwise FAIL.** Record the verdict, the assessor's name, and the time.

### Phase F — Depressurization and disconnect

26. **Depressurize using the release valve only**, slowly and in a controlled manner: crack the release valve open, let pressure fall, then open fully. Discharge to drain, away from personnel.
27. **Confirm the gauge reads 0 bar gauge.** Wait ~30 s for residual drainage/creep to settle, then re-confirm 0 bar gauge. If a separate manifold gauge and pump gauge are both fitted, both must read 0 bar gauge.
28. Open the high-point vent to confirm no residual pressure: gauge remains at 0 bar gauge and no flow exits.
29. **Only after 0 bar gauge is confirmed**, disconnect the pump hose and remove the manifold.
30. Drain and dry the manifold; remove the indicator paper; inspect for permanent deformation, weeping seals, or damaged threads. Record the inspection result.
31. Complete and sign the test log; attach it to the job record; remove the barrier and signage.

### If the test fails

Do not disconnect under pressure. Depressurize per steps 26–29, record the leak location and/or ΔP, repair/re-torque/re-seal as required, and restart from step 4 (full re-fill and re-vent). A retest is recorded on a new log.

## 5. Test log — as-run record

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Item | Water manifold, already connected |
| Component rating | 10.0 bar gauge |
| Target test pressure | 6.00 bar gauge (60% of rating) |
| Gauge / calibration | 0–10 bar gauge, ±0.5% FS, calibration current |
| Vent closed before pressurization | Yes (step 12) |
| Pump isolated before timer start | Yes (step 18) |
| Hold duration | 300 s |
| P₀ at start of isolated hold (t = 0 s) | 6.00 bar gauge |
| P₁ at end of hold (t = 300 s) | 5.90 bar gauge |
| Pressure drop ΔP = P₀ − P₁ | 0.10 bar |
| Water added during hold | None |
| Visible leakage during hold | None |

## 6. Acceptance assessment and verdict

**AC-1 — Pressure retention (ΔP ≤ 0.20 bar over 300 s).**
ΔP = 6.00 − 5.90 = **0.10 bar**. 0.10 bar ≤ 0.20 bar → **MET** (margin 0.10 bar, i.e. 50% of the allowance; equivalently P₁ = 5.90 bar gauge ≥ 5.80 bar gauge minimum).

**AC-2 — No visible leakage during the hold.**
No visible leakage recorded at any joint or component throughout the 300 s hold → **MET**.

Both criteria met.

### VERDICT: **PASS**

Notes (do not affect the verdict): the 0.10 bar drop is not accompanied by any visible leakage, and is consistent with elastic compliance of the manifold and/or a small ambient temperature decrease during the hold; ambient temperature was recorded per step 22 for traceability. The observed 0.10 bar drop is only twice a 0.05 bar gauge resolution — for future tests where tighter resolution of the drop is wanted, use a 0.01 bar-resolution digital gauge and record ambient temperature at both ends of the hold.

verdict.summary:
HYDROSTATIC LEAK-TEST PROCEDURE — CONNECTED WATER MANIFOLD ON A GUARDED BENCH

0. BASIS AND FIXED PARAMETERS
- Test pressure: 6.00 bar gauge (setpoint; it is also the required hold-start reading).
- Component rating: 10.0 bar gauge for all test components; 6.00 bar g is 0.60 of rating, i.e. within rating.
- Isolated hold time: 300 s, timed from the instant the hand pump is isolated.
- Acceptance: pressure drop <= 0.20 bar over the hold AND no visible water leakage during the hold (both required).
- Prohibition: no water addition during the 300 s hold.
- Gauge: in-date calibration, range 0-10 bar gauge or wider, resolution <= 0.01 bar, zero-checked against 0 bar gauge before the test.
- State at start: manifold already connected and unpressurized (gauge reads 0 bar gauge).

1. BENCH PREPARATION AND SAFETY (before filling)
1.1 Verify bench guarding: physical guard/barrier in place, any guard interlock closed, exclusion zone established. Keep all personnel clear of end caps, blank flanges and the release/jet path.
1.2 PPE per bench rules: safety glasses with side shields at minimum, face shield during pressurization and venting, gloves, closed footwear, long sleeves. Test performed by trained personnel only.
1.3 Confirm the manifold is connected, clamped/secured, and initially unpressurized: gauge reads 0 bar gauge.
1.4 Identify every vent, drain and test port on the manifold. Confirm the release valve is CLOSED and its discharge hose is routed and secured to the drain/collection point. Confirm the hand pump is connected and its isolation valve is ready to operate.
1.5 Record gauge ID, calibration due date and resolution in the log.

2. FILL AND VENT (air removal) — bench instruction
2.1 Open the high-point vent FULLY. All other vents/drain ports CLOSED.
2.2 Admit water through the fill/hand pump connection slowly, with the high-point vent open, so entrained air migrates to the high point.
2.3 Continue filling until bubble-free water exits the high-point vent continuously (steady stream, no entrained air). Record 'fill complete — bubble-free at high-point vent'.
2.4 Close the high-point vent. Verify that all other vents/drain ports are closed and tight.
2.5 NO PRESSURIZATION BEFORE THE HIGH-POINT VENT IS CLOSED.

3. PRESSURIZE
3.1 With the pump isolation valve open, raise pressure slowly and smoothly with the hand pump toward 6.00 bar gauge.
3.2 Allow pressure to stabilize, then make the final adjustment so the gauge reads 6.00 bar gauge. Do not overshoot the setpoint.
3.3 Do not open the release valve or vent during pressurization.

4. ISOLATE THE HAND PUMP AND START THE HOLD TIMER
4.1 Close the hand pump isolation valve FULLY to isolate the manifold from the pump. Do not operate the pump or that valve again during the hold.
4.2 Start the 300 s hold timer ONLY AFTER isolation is complete: t = 0 s is the instant the pump isolation valve is fully closed. The timer must NOT be started when 6.00 bar gauge is reached.
4.3 Record P_start = 6.00 bar gauge at t = 0 s.

5. ISOLATED HOLD — 300 s
5.1 Hold for 300 s. Record the actual elapsed time; the run is valid only if the full 300 s elapses after isolation.
5.2 DO NOT ADD WATER DURING THE HOLD: pump idle and isolated, fill connection closed, no pump strokes, no top-up, no make-up water from any source.
5.3 Do not operate the vent, the release valve, the pump isolation valve, or any other manifold valve during the hold.
5.4 Leakage observation (continuous during the hold): inspect the entire manifold — every joint, fitting, weld, packing/gland, end cap, gauge connection, hose and plug — for visible water leakage (drip, weep, mist, wetting). Use adequate lighting; for obscured joints use a mirror or borescope. Observe at minimum at t = 0 s, t = 150 s and t = 300 s with continuous watch between observations. Record either 'no visible water leakage' or the exact location, nature and time of each observed leak.
5.5 At t = 300 s record P_end on the same gauge.

6. ASSESS THE RESULT
6.1 Compute pressure drop: delta-P = P_start - P_end.
6.2 Evaluate AC-1 and AC-2 of Section 7. Both must be met for a PASS.
6.3 If the run is invalid under Section 7.3, record it as INVALID (not a fail) and repeat the test.

7. ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA
7.1 AC-1 — Pressure drop: delta-P = P_start - P_end <= 0.20 bar, measured over the 300 s isolated hold with no water added. A drop greater than 0.20 bar FAILS. (0.20 bar is the maximum permitted drop.)
7.2 AC-2 — Leakage: NO visible water leakage at any point on the manifold during the hold. Any visible water leakage FAILS.
7.3 Both AC-1 and AC-2 must be satisfied for PASS. Additionally: test pressure 6.00 bar gauge must be within the 10.0 bar gauge rating of all test components.
7.4 Invalid-run conditions (test void, repeat required): timer started before the pump was fully isolated; any water added during the hold; hold shorter than 300 s; hold-start pressure not 6.00 bar gauge; gauge out of calibration, un-zeroed, or resolution worse than 0.01 bar; isolation not maintained for the full hold.

8. DEPRESSURIZE AND DISCONNECT
8.1 After the result is assessed and recorded, stand clear of the release path and confirm the release-valve discharge hose is secured to the drain/collection point.
8.2 Open the RELEASE VALVE gradually to depressurize the manifold. Keep clear of end caps and any jet path; do not break any joint while pressure remains.
8.3 Confirm the gauge reads 0 bar gauge and remains stable at 0 bar gauge (no re-pressurization).
8.4 Only after 0 bar gauge is confirmed, close the release valve as required and disconnect the manifold. No disconnection before 0 bar gauge is confirmed.

9. VERDICT FOR THIS LOG
Log data: P_start = 6.00 bar gauge at t = 0 s (hold start, after pump isolation); P_end = 5.90 bar gauge at t = 300 s; no visible water leakage throughout the hold; 300 s hold with no water added.
Calculation: delta-P = 6.00 - 5.90 = 0.10 bar.
AC-1: 0.10 bar <= 0.20 bar — SATISFIED (0.10 bar below the limit).
AC-2: no visible water leakage — SATISFIED.
Validity: isolation before timer start, no water added, full 300 s hold, 6.00 bar g at hold start — all satisfied.
VERDICT: PASS.

10. REQUIRED LOG RECORD
Test ID; date/time; operator name and signature; manifold/component identification (serial numbers) and 10.0 bar g rating; gauge ID, calibration due date, resolution and zero check; water and ambient temperature; fill completion evidence (bubble-free water at high-point vent) and vent closed; pressurization to 6.00 bar gauge; isolation timestamp (= t = 0 s) and timer start timestamp; hold duration 300 s; P_start = 6.00 bar gauge; P_end (5.90 bar gauge for this log); delta-P = 0.10 bar; leakage observations with times (none observed for this log); AC-1 and AC-2 results; run validity; verdict (PASS for this log); depressurization timestamp; confirmation of 0 bar gauge before disconnect; remarks.
